messages:
maria: Quick heads-up — ran longflow KV cache suite overnight. Seeing steady memory creep on 30k+ token sessions. Not obvious eviction triggers.

 tom: new regression or expected? did baseline show same?

 maria: baseline from two weeks ago (commit a1b2c3) didn't grow past ~4.1GB. current build (main@d2e3f4) hits 7.6GB by 50k tokens. repro script attached.

 maria: ```bash
 # run single-worker longflow synth
 ./bench/run_kvcache --suite longflow --seq-lens 1024,2048,4096,16384 --clients 8 --duration 3h --trace=kvcache.trace
 ```

 kevin: can you paste the top of kvcache.trace? the paging/evict events?

 maria: pasted logs:
 `[KVCACHE] alloc_page id=142 size=256MB owner=decoder`
 `[KVCACHE] evict_page id=13 score=0.2 reason=age`
 `[KVCACHE] reuse_page id=13 owner=decoder`
 `[KVCACHE] alloc_page id=220 size=256MB owner=decoder`
 `[KVCACHE] mem_total=4103MB mem_total=7601MB` (snip)

 sara: hmm "reuse_page" right after evict_page suggests fragmentation — pages being partially reused but still staying allocated? Could be not freeing backing memory until compaction.

 raj: I saw similar in kv-reuse bug earlier — kernel selection path for quantized attention caused extra pinned slices. Maybe related.

 kevin: let's run the microbenchmark that forces tiny fragmented writes. I have a quick script:
 ```py
 # make many small KV writes to force fragmentation
 for i in range(100000):
   kv.put(key=f\"user:{i%4096}:pos:{i}\", value=rand_bytes(128))
 ```

 bench-bot: scheduled job 1760001300 started: kvcache-frag-micro (expect ~2h)

 maria: also noticed latency tail increases ~20ms when mem >6GB, likely due to background compaction. need to confirm.

 tom: can you capture pmap /proc/<pid>/smaps and malloc_stats around the plateau? that would help distinguish kernel vs user allocations.

 maria: done — attached snippet:
 `VmRSS: 6123456 kB`
 `AnonHugePages: 0 kB`
 `RssFile: 102400 kB`
 `HeapTotal: 1.4GB`
 `malloc_trim called but no free returned`

 sara: malloc_trim not freeing suggests fragmentation in libc arena. We might be holding many small allocations; switching to jemalloc/tcmalloc could help.

 raj: but we rely on jemalloc in Dedicated builds already, right? Confirmed in Dockerfile?

 kevin: main builds default to glibc malloc for perf tests. Dedicated images use jemalloc. That difference could explain regression: our test harness is using main (glibc) and fragmentation appears there.

 maria: run with jemalloc option: `LD_PRELOAD=/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libjemalloc.so ./bench/..` — tried that, mem stabilizes at ~4.3GB. So probably allocator fragmentation.

 tom: good catch. Need to add jemalloc to CI kvcache longflow suite and note platform differences. :thumbsup: 

 sara: also found a KV code path that keeps free list nodes in thread-local caches without size culling. If jemalloc reduces fragmentation, the underlying leak means we still have high virtual allocations.

 kevin: created PR to add max_tcache_bytes for the allocator and added explicit periodic release of big chunks. PR link: https://example.com/pull/987

 bench-bot: job 1760001300 completed: failure=0, peak_rss=4.35GB, notes=fragmentation reduced with jemalloc

 maria: next steps: (1) add jemalloc to longflow CI, (2) add microbench frag test to regression harness, (3) instrument kvcache to emit compact/alloc histograms per minute, (4) test on Dedicated images.

 raj: assignable? I'll take (4). @sara can you own (3)? @tom (1), @kevin (2).

 sara: on it, will add histograms and a quick grafana dashboard.

 tom: I'll update CI matrix and infra docs; may require packaging jemalloc in test image.

 maria: thanks all. leaving traces+bench logs in /bench/artifacts/1760001234/*

 infra-bot: reminder — please attach the bench artifacts to the ticket: INFRA-4821

 maria: filed INFRA-4821 with logs & links, tagging this thread.

 kevin: follow-up: still want to add a long-duration run that mixes very long contexts (100k tokens) and short chats to stress reuse patterns. I'll open an RFC.

 maria: perfect. closing for now, will reopen if regression recurs.
